system.name: ADAngel
system.one_liner: a workload-aware framework that adaptively selects mixed-precision GEMM/GEMV kernel strategies to accelerate arbitrary-precision quantized (APQ) LLM inference

components.name: Transformer
components.role: a standard decoder-only Transformer block (Attention, Add & Norm, FFN, Add & Norm) repeated between input and output tokens

components.name: Attention
components.role: self-attention sublayer whose Wq/Wk/Wv weights are quantized in the middle panel

components.name: FFN
components.role: feed-forward sublayer whose weights/activations are quantized in the middle panel

components.name: LLM Quant.
components.role: quantizes Wq/Wk/Wv from FP32 to Int4 via a single Quant operator

components.name: Mixed-Precision Quant.
components.role: quantizes weights W to Int4 and activations A to Int8 separately, the arbitrary-precision quantization (APQ) scheme this paper targets

components.name: On-the-fly Padding
components.role: existing strategy that pads Int4 weights to Int8 before an Int8 Matmul, then dequantizes

components.name: LUT-based Strategy
components.role: existing strategy that precomputes a lookup table indexed to evaluate the mixed-precision product without padding

summary: This is a background figure from the ADAngel paper (ADAngel itself, a workload-aware framework for accelerating arbitrary-precision quantized LLM inference, is shown separately in Figure 6). It builds up the concepts ADAngel targets in three columns. Left: a standard decoder-only Transformer block (Attention, Add & Norm, FFN, repeated, ending in SoftMax/Sampling). Middle: how post-training quantization converts FP32 weights, and in arbitrary-precision quantization also activations, to low-bit-width Int4/Int8 representations, contrasting uniform LLM quantization with mixed-precision quantization where weights and activations get different bit-widths. Right: two existing ways to execute the resulting mixed-precision GEMM/GEMV on edge hardware without native support: On-the-fly Padding, which upcasts the lower-precision operand before an Int8 matmul, and a LUT-based Strategy, which precomputes a lookup table instead.
